Public Portion 
 1. Discussion of FY27 Tax Rate Information with Approved Values 
On November 12, 2026, the Finance/Tax Rate Committee, chaired by Councilor Zaida Govan, 
met to review the Fiscal Year 2027 property tax classification and proposed tax rates. Board of 
Assessors Chair Jessica Guerra presented updated property valuations, certified new growth of 
approximately $8.7 million, and a total taxable property value of approximately $15.7 billion. 
The average single-family home assessment increased from $275,200 to $291,500. The 
presentation also included the City's Targeted Tax Relief Program, which received 51 
applications as of the meeting date, with the application deadline extended to December 4, 2026. 
 
The committee reviewed the proposed maximum tax shift, with a residential factor of 0.7846, 
resulting in a proposed residential tax rate of $15.23 and a commercial, industrial, and personal 
property rate of $33.96 per $1,000 of assessed value. The Mayor's proposed $5 million tax levy 
offset included $3 million in free cash and $2 million in interest earnings. Under the proposal, 
the average single-family property tax bill would increase by approximately $185. Discussion 
addressed rising property assessments, utility costs, the distribution of the tax burden, and the 
importance of residential and commercial development. Councilor Govan indicated that she
would request a meeting with Eversource to discuss whether utility property tax costs are passed 
on to customers. 
 
A motion was made by Diana Szynal and seconded by Ronald Molina-Brantley to accept the 
proposed tax rates presented by the Board of Assessors, including the Mayor's proposed offset. 
The motion passed, advancing the committee's recommendation for full City Council 
consideration. The City Council's tax classification vote is scheduled for November 24, 2026. 
The meeting adjourned at 6:00 p.m.
